newsitem.title: USA: 12th tropical depression forms in Caribbean.
newsitem.headline: 12th tropical depression forms in Caribbean.

text.p: The 12th tropical depression of the Atlantic hurricane season formed in the western Caribbean Tuesday, and threatened to become Tropical Storm Lili later in the day, National Hurricane Center said.
At 0800 EDT/1200 GMT, the depression's center was near latitude 15.5 north and longitude 82.5 west, about 165 miles (264 km) southeast of Swan Island in the northwest Caribbean.
The system was moving northwest at nearly eight mph (13 kph), and this is expected to continue during the day, forecasters said.

Its maximum sustained winds were near 35 mph (56 kph) and the system was expected to strengthen to become a tropical storm later on Tuesday. Tropical depressions become tropical storms when maximum sustained winds reach 39 mph (62 kph).
